answer: A seat must be backed by its own piece of silicon. Each epoch the seat asks its secure enclave for a quote over the current challenge; the quote carries an endorsement key burned into one onyx die and a monotonic counter that advances every time it signs. The network accepts one pigment per die per epoch, so a second seat claiming the same hardware is refused, and the counter's ripple exposes any attempt to fork a cloned key. Running N fakes requires N dies with distinct keys, each bought, powered and kept online, so the attacker pays a hardware bill that never amortizes across identities.
